changes: Inline LogView collection setup into its sole setLogcat caller; remove always-false job/source guards and redundant cancelled-scope precheck, preserving lifecycle-owner handling and stop/detach cleanup.
Restore public Process.asFlow/readText/readLines helpers byte-for-byte from upstream baseline; only actual Logcat consumeOutput paths receive owned-process lifecycle changes.

Replace two unconditional process releases, AtomicReference and production IdentityHashMap error graph with local releaseOnce state and a short CancellationException cause chain only. The watcher and outer finally are both retained because they cover blocked reads and cancellation before IO dispatch respectively.

Keep the original bufferedReader.use scope; it manages reader resource lifetime and adds close failures to the actual original read exception before coroutine recovery. One process destroy/release operation does not imply exactly one underlying input.close call.

Remove newly introduced arbitrary 2s clear / 5s deploy-log timeout policies and their duplicated timeout branches; keep cancellation propagation, IO-owned log collection and error fallback/diagnostics.

Retarget process tests at the actual owned consumeOutput primitive instead of the reverted generic helper behavior. Remove redundant generic flow/double-destroy cases; add cancellation-before-IO and original-read-plus-single-cleanup-failure contracts. Strengthen shared fake process destruction checks to exactly one.
required_boundaries: A cancellation watcher must release the actual process on an independent elastic cleanup view while a read blocks, including when the normal IO dispatcher has parallelism one.
The outer finally must also own a process created immediately before cancellation prevents the IO reader from starting.
releaseOnce marks state before suspending. withContext(IO) structurally waits for its watcher child before the outer finally; limitedParallelism(1) alone is not a mutex spanning suspensions.
The NonCancellable job boundary must surround the dispatcher switch and its return, so a cancelled caller cannot skip diagnostic attachment on a normal cross-dispatch return.
With assertions/debug recovery enabled, the short CancellationException cause restoration is necessary to attach cleanup failure to the stable original cancellation seen by async.await.
Actual process release still attempts other stream closes after a destroy/getter/close failure and observes child exit with the existing bounded cooperative wait.
Keep subscriber-before-producer ordering, stale job identity checks, API21 short command/PID-column/LF framing behavior, display/pending capacity budgets and explicit export omission notice.

negative_controls.notes: Diagnostic source variants precede restoration of the preexisting reader.use statement. Exact final host5 source separately passes the same strict caught-exception graph contract and original read/close contract.
